executive_assessment.text: Djobel adds a detailed historical flood, dike, mobility and contested safer-land case; it cannot represent Guinea-Bissau as a whole.
Hydromet projects face financial and political constraints, while WFP service and resilience commitments remain separately dated plans/capacity context.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-04 reports: CCDR says rising seas are forcing Djobel to retreat from the coast and reigniting historical interethnic conflicts over land use and resources.

Source dated 2024-04 reports: Flooding puts national roads N1, N2 and N5 at risk; rainy-season road impassability restricts rural access to markets, water, schools and health care, especially for women.

Source dated 2022-09-12 reports: In Djobel, 2017 storm surges, heavy rain and high-tide waves destroyed most rice-field infrastructure; ten families became houseless and damaged dikes left some children travelling to school by canoe or swimming.
The Djobel researchers describe an upland territorial dispute with neighbouring Arame that constrained efforts to establish safer settlement space.

Source dated 2022-09-12 reports: After years of requests for assistance and the 2017 flood and dike rupture, the authors report no effective technical or financial support for climate adaptation from state, NGOs or donors.
Source dated 2022-09-12 reports: Most young people return to Djobel seasonally for field work, leaving dike repair and maintenance to a diminishing number who stay.

Source dated 2024-07 reports: INM-GB operated 19 classic weather stations, only 8 operational and none automatic; Bissau Airport, Bolama and Bafatá issued observations every three hours during daytime.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 21 of 21 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
NC4 explicitly reserves all rights and requires prior authorization; only original paraphrases, not source text, are recorded.
The 2026 NDC PDF labels itself draft even though the UNFCCC registry marks the submission active.
The earlier NDC uses a different coastal-zone estimate than NDC 3.0; its projection and population figures are kept source-specific rather than combined.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The UN Common Country Analysis PDF returned HTTP 530 and the UNICEF 2025 regional situation report exceeded browser size limits; no claims use search-indexed text from either source.
The Djobel research is a detailed single-village case and should not be generalized to Guinea-Bissau; conflict history includes qualitative accounts and cited historical records.
The CCDR's farmer-herder and Djobel pathways are source-stated but do not provide local conflict incidence or independently estimate climate attribution.
The hydromet diagnostic and WFP plan document capacity constraints and commitments, but not the current reach or effectiveness of last-mile warnings and services.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
